issues.legal_issue: A constitutional challenge to land abolition measures cannot be founded on a dispute over an agreement made during the integration of a former State.
material_facts: The former ruler entered into agreements with the Dominion of India in connection with the transfer of administration of the State.
The challengers relied on those agreements to oppose the successor government's abolition of land interests.
issues.conclusion: The challengers could not rely on the agreements to raise the dispute because Article 363 barred it.
issues.legal_principle: Article 363 bars courts from entertaining disputes arising out of agreements made in connection with the integration of States. The Court relied on Maharaj Umeg Singh v. State of Bombay, 1955-2 SCR 164: (AIR 1955 SC 540).

predicates.constitutional_land_reform_challenge: A person brings a constitutional challenge to measures abolishing land interests.
predicates.claim_depends_on_state_integration_agree: The challenger bases the claim on an agreement made in connection with the integration of a former State.

issues.definition: When a constitutional land-reform challenge depends on an agreement made in connection with State integration, the dispute is barred.

issues.legal_issue: An agreement to honour prior contracts does not prevent a successor government from abolishing land interests as part of its general policy.
material_facts: The agreement provided that earlier contracts would be honoured except where they were repugnant to applicable law or inconsistent with the successor government's general policy.
The successor government adopted a general policy of abolishing land estates throughout the State.
A separate agreement clause concerned lifetime cash grants to specified members of the ruling family, and the claimant relying on it was not on the attached list.
issues.conclusion: The agreements did not protect the land interests from abolition; the clause concerning family grants did not apply to the claimant.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement's express exception for contracts inconsistent with the successor government's general policy meant that land-related contracts could not defeat its general abolition policy. The clause concerning grants and allowances was limited to the specified family members and cash allowances charged on State revenue.

predicates.land_interest_claim_based_on_prior_contr: A claimant asserts that a prior contract protects a land interest from abolition.
predicates.successor_adopted_general_abolition_poli: The successor government adopted a general policy of abolishing land interests of the relevant kind.

issues.definition: A prior contract does not prevent abolition when the claimant relies on it to protect a land interest and the successor government has adopted a general policy of abolishing such interests.

issues.legal_issue: Allowing the executive to extend an existing law to different geographical areas at different times does not amount to excessive delegation of essential legislative functions.
material_facts: The legislature reserved power for the government to apply an existing land-reform law to areas where it had not initially applied.
The government later applied the law to the former State's territory.
issues.conclusion: The delegation of power to extend the law geographically was not excessive.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may leave to the executive the application of an enacted law to different geographical areas at different times, having regard to relevant considerations. The Court considered section 2(1) of the Abolition Act.

predicates.challenge_to_geographical_extension_powe: A constitutional challenge contends that executive authority to extend a law to additional areas delegates essential legislative functions.
predicates.legislature_enacted_law_before_executive: The legislature enacted the law and left the executive to decide when it would apply in different geographical areas.

issues.definition: When the legislature has enacted a law and left the executive to select the areas and times of its application, the geographical extension power is not excessive delegation.

issues.legal_issue: A retrospective legislative amendment to a statutory definition governs pending litigation and may remove an objection that an earlier notification changed the definition.
material_facts: A notification applying the land-reform law to the territory had altered the statutory definition of an estate.
A later amendment substituted a definition that applied retrospectively from before the notification and covered the relevant land interests.
The amendment contained no express saving for pending litigation.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective amendment removed the basis of the definition-related challenge, and no exception for pending litigation could be implied.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the retrospective terms of the 1958 amending Act and held that a saving for pending litigation could not be implied. It cited K. C. Mukherjee v. Mt. Ramratan Kuer, 63 Ind App 47: (AIR 1936 PC 49).

predicates.pending_challenge_to_application_of_land: A challenge to the application of a land-reform law remains pending when a later enactment takes effect.
predicates.retrospective_amendment_covers_disputed_: A later enactment retrospectively changes the relevant definition so that it covers the land interests in dispute.
predicates.no_pending_case_saving_expressed: The later enactment does not expressly preserve pending cases from the effect of its retrospective change.

issues.definition: A pending challenge is governed by a retrospective definition that covers the disputed land when the later enactment does not expressly preserve pending cases.

issues.legal_issue: Holders of leases granting them an independent interest in land are lessees, not mere managers, and a law applying to those leases may determine them.
material_facts: The instruments described the arrangements as leases and the holders as lessees.
The holders were to invest their own money, pay a share of profits as revenue, and had heritable interests.
The State could take over direct management if the lease conditions were not fulfilled.
issues.conclusion: The holders were not mere managers, and the Thekedari Act applied to and could determine their leases.
issues.legal_principle: The lease definition in section 2(6), and the provisions for determination and its consequences in sections 3 and 4 of the Thekedari Act, applied to leases of this kind. The Court assessed the substance and terms of the arrangements, including the holders' independent interests and obligations.

predicates.challenge_to_termination_of_land_arrange: A person challenges the application of a law that terminates land arrangements of a particular kind.
predicates.arrangement_grants_independent_land_inte: The arrangement gives the holder an interest in the land rather than appointing the holder solely to act for the State.
predicates.holder_invests_own_money: The holder is required to invest the holder's own money in the land or its development.
predicates.holder_has_heritable_interest: The holder's interest under the arrangement is heritable.

issues.definition: A holder who has an independent, heritable land interest and must invest personal funds is treated as a lessee whose arrangement may be reached by a law governing such leases.

issues.legal_issue: A law determining land leases is valid when the legislature has authority over the subject and the law complies with the constitutional requirement for compensation.
material_facts: The law determined leases and provided for compensation to the lessees.
The challengers did not argue that the compensation was inadequate.
The Court found the law within the legislature's authority over land matters and compliant with the constitutional compensation requirement.
issues.conclusion: The Thekedari Act was within legislative power and complied with Article 31(2), and was valid.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Entry 18 of List II of the Seventh Schedule as conferring legislative authority over the subject and held that the Act complied with Article 31(2).

rule.if: challenge_to_land_lease_abolition_law and legislature_has_authority_over_land_matters and law_provides_compensation and compensation_adequacy_not_contested

predicates.challenge_to_land_lease_abolition_law: A person challenges a law that abolishes or determines land leases.
predicates.legislature_has_authority_over_land_matt: The legislature has authority over the subject matter regulated by the law.
predicates.law_provides_compensation: The law provides compensation to persons whose lease interests it determines.
predicates.compensation_adequacy_not_contested: The challenger does not dispute the adequacy of the compensation provided.

issues.definition: A land-lease abolition law is valid when the legislature has authority over the subject, the law provides compensation, and the adequacy of that compensation is not contested.
